Background There is no evidence of the use of beetroot juice with a previously recommended dose of nitrate (NO3) (> 300 mg) on the cardiovascular performance during and recovery following exercise in postmenopausal women with systemic arterial hypertension (SAH). Methods We will investigate the effects of beetroot juice rich in NO3 acutely (800 mg) and during a week with daily doses (400 mg) on blood pressure, heart rate (HR), cardiac autonomic control, endothelial function, inflammatory, hormonal, and stress biomarkers oxidative stress and enzymes involved in nitric oxide synthesis and mitochondrial regulation, under resting conditions, as well as mediated by submaximal aerobic exercise sessions. Through a randomized, crossover, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial, 25 physically inactive women with SAH will undergo an acute and 1-week trial, each with two intervention protocols: (1) placebo and (2) beetroot, in which will ingest beet juice with or without NO3 in its composition with a 7-day washout interval. On collection days, exercise will be performed on a treadmill for 40 min at a speed corresponding to 65–70% of VO2peak. The collection of variables (cardiovascular, autonomic, and blood samples for molecular analyses) of the study will take place at rest (135 min after ingestion of the intervention), during exercise (40 min), and in the effort recovery stage (during 60 min) based on previously validated protocols. The collections were arranged so that the measurement of one variable does not interfere with the other and that they have adequate intervals between them. Discussion The results of this research may help in the real understanding of the nutritional compounds capable of generating safety to the cardiovascular system during physical exercise, especially for women who are aging and who have cardiovascular limitations (e.g., arterial hypertension) to perform physical exercise. Therefore, our results will be able to help specific nutritional recommendations to optimize cardiovascular health. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05384340. Registered on May 20, 2022. extracted_data.document_summary: This study protocol describes a randomized, crossover, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial investigating the acute and 1-week effects of nitrate-rich beetroot juice on cardiovascular performance, autonomic control, endothelial function, and a range of molecular biomarkers (inflammatory, hormonal, oxidative stress, nitric oxide synthesis, and mitochondrial regulation) in physically inactive postmenopausal women (aged 50-70) with systemic arterial hypertension, both at rest, during submaximal aerobic exercise, and throughout recovery. The aim is to provide nutritional recommendations for optimizing cardiovascular health.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Dietary supplementation with nitrate-rich beetroot juice combined with standardized submaximal aerobic exercise.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: Nitrate-rich beetroot juice will be administered acutely at 140 mL (800 mg nitrate) on the first day, followed by a daily dose of 70 mL (400 mg nitrate) for 6 subsequent days. A placebo (nitrate-free) juice will serve as control. Exercise consists of a 40-minute treadmill session at a speed corresponding to 65-70% of VO2peak. The study employs a randomized, crossover, triple-blind, placebo-controlled design with a 7-day washout period between intervention protocols. Previous research indicated lower doses (200-400 mg nitrate) were insufficient for acute cardiovascular effects, leading to the optimized dosages used here. Additionally, 40 g of whey protein will be provided before executing experimental protocols.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Systolic Blood Pressure reduced by -4.95 mmHg (95% CI: -8.88; -1.01) with NO3-rich beetroot juice supplementation (from previous studies). For this study, not yet quantified as this is a study protocol; quantitative/statistical data will be collected at rest (135 min after ingestion), during exercise (40 min), and during 60 min of recovery.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: lower (endogenous NO); higher (exogenous NO/NO3); produced/transformed (NO2); to be investigated (enzymes protocol)
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Endogenous NO reduced by abrupt drop in estrogen levels in postmenopausal women and with aging. Exogenous NO increased via nitrate ingestion (NO3 transformed to NO after reduction to NO2 by oral bacteria and reaction with low pH in the stomach). NO3 increased to cause physiological effects only after 4 to 6 days of beet juice ingestion (> 300 mg of nitrate). NO2 partially reduced from ingested NO3 by oral bacteria; subsequently reacts with low pH in the stomach to be transformed into Nitric Oxide (NO). For enzymes, not yet quantified as this is a study protocol; quantitative/statistical data will be collected. Plasma nitrite will be quantified using a Nitric Oxide Analyzer (Sievers NOATM – model 280i) to indirectly quantify nitric oxide (NO) concentration.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Endothelial relaxing factor; crucial role in vasodilation. Precursor to Nitrite (NO2) and then Nitric Oxide (NO) in the exogenous pathway. Intermediate in the conversion of Nitrate to Nitric Oxide. Catalyze NO production, involved in vasodilation, blood flow, anti-inflammatory processes.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Postmenopausal non-reproductive phase, aging, ingestion of nitrate-rich beetroot juice. Acute (800 mg) and 1-week daily (400 mg) nitrate-rich beetroot juice intake during resting conditions and submaximal aerobic exercise (40 min at 65-70% VO2peak) and recovery in postmenopausal women with systemic arterial hypertension (SAH). Analysis before and after exercise to attest effects due to increased nitrate intake.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Decreased NO production contributes to systemic arterial hypertension (SAH) and cardiovascular/cerebrovascular diseases; increased production improves cardiovascular functioning through vasodilation. Increased NO3 bioavailability leads to hypotensive effects and improved cardiovascular responses. Crucial for increasing NO production, playing a role in vasodilation. Indicator of nitric oxide bioavailability, endothelial health, and vasoregulatory capacity.
